text:
Two back to back reviews by Richard in the last two days? I'm confused, I thought we still had a couple of weeks until Christmas. 

1:52, 2:25 and 2:43 this is amazing stuff, this is new state of the art in benchmarking, can't wait to see it all in action! And 4:14 Man, I can't believe what I am seeing and hearing here, this is outstanding!!! Years in the past I've criticized, even pretty harshly, some of Richard's hardware reviews, but since a long while now he has been leaning towards a way more balanced coverage, "just" is the right word here. See, if you bring in the bad stuff, especially when done in bad faith, I'm going to be absolutely merciless with my critique, but the same way if you bring in the good stuff I am going to shower you with praise.

Guiding gamers towards better configs, better way to spend their money, better way to enjoy their games, which is also the goal of the "optimized settings" thingy, no? It's the same underlying principle and I am super stocked to see this is the direction DF wants to embrace for the future. So happy to see this.

Coming to Intel GPUs: I've been pretty critical with their 1st gen, a no-buy for me, but I have to say I find this 2nd gen to be kind of impressive. First off, props to Rich for addressing the driver situation, 2022 Richard wouldn't have done that, so again massive props for the change of direction, then onto the B580: yes it has some hitches here and there, drivers definitely need to improve, especially in older titles, but for an entry level GPU? At this price? If I was in the market in this price bracket, I'd definitely go with the Battlemage. 

Rich still stresses how far ahead Nvidia still is with their features (19:03), but this is perhaps the only point where I would not completely agree with him: I wouldn't necessarily be concerned about quality when it comes to DLSS vs XeSS, the latter does great on XMX; what I would be more concerned about is definitely support, but even there, looking forward we need to consider also TSR into the equation, since a boatload of games are coming on UE5, so that makes things way more relaxed in terms of coverage, in my opinion. There are plenty of valid alternatives, other engines like Decima doing their own thing, I am not sure DLSS still holds this crucial value when considering a GPU, not anymore. 

Anyhow, thanks for the review, good stuff.

text: Consoles use APUs (CPU and GPU on the same die) and have been doing so for a long time. This is cheaper and comes with other advantages, like requiring less space, producing less heat, etc. Mid-cycle upgrades (like PS5 Pro) are far more lucrative anyway than upgradeable hardware; manufacturers don't have any interest in lowering cost to the customer. People are also expecting a plug and play experience with their games on console, with few graphics settings to worry about. The moment you're introducing even a handful of GPU options, both consumers and developers will be up in arms. Developers are already constantly complaining about Xbox Series S and how much work this one lower end variant means to them.
